questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the file state that measures to reduce the loss are still to be taken (not yet carried out)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the file state that the measures could not wait for the insurer's instruction because of imminent danger (Gefahr im Verzug)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the policy, or the file, show that the policy does not include the separate supplementary insurance for simple theft away from home (einfacher Diebstahl auswärts)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the file state that the original purchase vouchers for all of the stolen or damaged items cannot be obtained, or only at considerable cost (not even as a duplicate from the seller)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the file state that traces of the theft (for example pry marks, a broken lock, window or container) have been removed or altered, or are to be removed or altered, by the policyholder or on their behalf, for example by repair or cleaning?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Is a bicycle among the stolen or damaged items?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Does the file state that household contents were stolen or damaged by a theft outside the insured location that was neither a burglary (the thief forcibly entered the building or a room of it, or broke open a container in it, or unlocked it with the correct keys or codes that the thief had obtained by burglary or robbery; a vehicle is not a container) or a robbery (theft under threat or use of violence against the policyholder or a member of the household, or while they could not resist because of unconsciousness, accident or death; pickpocketing and trick theft are not robbery)?

text:
Dear Mr Schneider,

Please find attached three documents for my claim: the police report from the gendarmerie in Yverdon, a copy of my CSS policy, and the list of what was stolen.

As you'll see in the policy, I have the extra cover for simple theft away from home. My sister Olivia Tanner talked me into it when I renewed in February, and I'm glad she did.

No bike is involved in this, by the way. It was all things I was carrying.

There is one point I'm unsure about. The police told me there's a small chance they can trace my phone if it gets switched on, and that if I block it now they lose that chance. My provider says the opposite, block it at once. I haven't decided yet which advice to follow, and the phone is still unblocked for the moment. If you have a view on that, I'd be glad to hear it.

You'll want receipts, and I have to disappoint you there: I don't have a single one. The phone and the watch were bought in England years ago, the sunglasses and the wallet were presents. Nobody can give me a duplicate for any of them.

As for what happened: on Wednesday 21 October 2026 I took the 17:15 train from Yverdon to Lausanne. It was packed and I stood by the door with my handbag over my shoulder. When I got off in Lausanne the bag was open and my wallet, phone, watch and sunglasses were gone. I never felt a thing. I went back to Yverdon and reported it that same evening. The total is about CHF 7,100.

Kind regards,
Clara Keller
Wiesenstrasse 45, Yverdon-les-Bains
